boundary: Pure editShowClipV2 ordinary linked duplication, provisional codec reopen, effective Group projection, routed Layout availability, and generated Fast/Precise replay
invariants: A linked duplicate creates exactly one ordinary Clip and no Pattern instance, instance-track owner or Transition; source and duplicate use the same runtime identity.

The caller supplies complete fresh identities for the new Clip, all copied appearance keys, all source Clip-owned tracks and every copied keyframe; missing, extraneous, blank, duplicate or owned identities refuse atomically.

Only copied appearance times, Clip-track activation and Clip-track key times shift by the placement delta; duration, sampling, appearance values, entry policy, easing, source choreography and instance animation remain unchanged.

Admission validates the complete result across ordinary and materialized-Group occupancy and every intersected Layout occurrence; half-open adjacency is valid and any overlap or unavailable Zone refuses.
Changed output is unaliased and reports only the new Clip and copied track identities; refusal returns the original record identity and empty affected collections.
partitions: Fresh versus blank, owned, duplicate, missing and extraneous Clip/appearance/track/key identities, including an ID already owned by a different Property target.
Safe integral in-range placement versus negative, fractional, past-Show-End and overflow placement.
Existing destination Zone/Layer versus missing Zone, missing Layer and Layer owned by another Zone.
Exact ordinary and materialized-Group adjacency versus one-millisecond materialized overlap.
No Transition versus an attached source Transition that must remain byte-equivalent and must not be copied.
One Layout versus a later routed Layout occurrence with the destination Zone present or unavailable.
Every Clip target form: opacity, view, transform, aperture and Effect, with instance animation present but uncopied.
Continue versus Restart entry policy, with ordinary and effective Group sharers on the same Pattern instance.
Fast versus Fidelity generated replay of a nonlinear copied Clip track and the second shared-runtime Restart.
sequences: Duplicate one Restart Clip at exact adjacency, reopen, derive two Restart events, and verify one unchanged Pattern instance plus one unchanged instance-time-scale track.
Duplicate beside a later materialized Group use, observe three effective users, then move the Group one millisecond earlier and require atomic collision refusal.
Duplicate into a second Layout occurrence, then replace that occurrence with a Layout lacking the destination Zone and require availability refusal.
Attach an incoming Transition to the source, duplicate after it, and compare the complete Transition collection byte-for-byte.
Serialize, reopen, prepare, compile and replay the source midpoint and duplicate midpoint in Fast and Fidelity modes.
oracles: Literal Clip, Pattern-instance, Property-track, Group and Transition collections plus exact affected IDs and unchanged input equality.
validateShowRecordV2 before each topology operation and after provisional serialization/reopen of each accepted result.
effectiveShowInstanceUseCountV2 observes the ordinary and materialized Group users without any new runtime.
deriveShowRestartEventsV2 exposes source and duplicate entries on the same instance at their exact contribution starts.

evaluateShowPropertyTrackV2 proves the copied nonlinear midpoint; generated Fast/Fidelity frames show that value and exported state exposes one shared runtime whose call counter resets at the duplicate entry.
